newsitem.title: FRANCE: Full text of statement by BoF governor Trichet.
newsitem.headline: Full text of statement by BoF governor Trichet.

text.p: Following is a translation of the statement issued by Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet on Friday. It is an unofficial translation by Reuters.
The monetary policy council, which met yesterday, decided not to change the official interest rates of the Bank of France.

The Bank of France is unshakeably committed to the stability of the franc in the group of the most credible European currencies, which comprise in particular the franc, the mark, the guilder, the Belgian franc, the Danish crown and the Austrian schilling. This exchange rate stability is part of the monetary policy council's policy. It is enshrined in the European policy of the President of the Republic and the Prime Minister and the strategic goal of Economic and Monetary Union decided by the President.

Naturally, nothing could justify a depreciation of the franc versus the other most credible currencies of the exchange rate mechanism, with a French economy which will have the third largest current account surplus in the world this year.

The credibility of our currency has allowed us to achieve for the benefit of out economy the third lowest market interest rates in the world. The French people have great confidence in the solidity of their currency. That confidence is an important and very positive factor for the recovery in our economy, which is currently underway, as is shown by the latest surveys by the Bank of France and the latest publications by INSEE (national statistics institute).

Should a reminder be needed, there is only one monetary policy council. It is the monetary policy council, a collegiate of nine people whose independence is guaranteed by law, which safeguards the currency on behalf of all French people. The monetary policy council has only one voice as a collegiate. It is the voice of its president, governor, and spokesman, as is the case for all the other major independent central banks in the world. Mr Greenspan and Mr Tietmeyer give the position of the Frederal Reserve and the Bundesbank as do I for the Bank of France.

In Paris, as in Frankfurt, as in Washington, the members of the council speak in a personal capacity. They clearly have the right to do so within the limits of our independent status, given our appreciation of the overriding interest which the law requires of us, that is to defend monetary stability.
